quest.title: White Horse's Leisurely Journey
quest.description: After the Lantern Rite, you decide to pay Zibai a visit...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x575, Primogem x60, Mora x53900, Guide to Gold x5, Recipe: Crispy Spring Rolls x1, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x12

chapter.num: A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon: Epilogue
chapter.title: White Horse's Leisurely Journey

talks.objective: Wait until the morning of the day after tomorrow

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You follow the young lady and settle in for the night at the Lu family residence in Qiaoying Village...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You enjoy a quiet night's sleep, and in the morning, you return together to the tea garden...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: An incredible sight awaits you...

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: The t—t—tea tree...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, your tea baby is all grown up!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Indeed. It has grown into a mature tea tree that can stand tall in the face of wind and rain.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: H—How... how is this possible?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It must be the work of the White Horse Adeptus! Your prayer must have moved her!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Perhaps she heard your prayer and chose to answer the call.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: ...She once saved my great-great-great-great... great-grandmother. This time, she's saved me...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's incredible! Your family must be blessed by the White Horse Adeptus!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: I guess so... I need to tell everyone the news right away!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They should unground you now, right?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: They'd better! Since this is the will of the White Horse Adeptus, I don't see how they could object!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Go! And if you run into any more trouble, call out to the White Horse Adeptus, just like yesterday.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Thank you so much!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pfft... Paimon really thought you were going to use adeptal energy to make the tea baby grow, Zibai!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: When an adeptus exerts effort — consuming their energy — is that not using adeptal energy?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn* Alright, alright. What are we doing out here in the middle of the night?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: We're here to help Lu Xiangxiang fulfill her wish, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can you really make the tea baby grow?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: It won't be easy, but there are ways.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: There. It's grown.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! You just transplanted a tea tree from over there!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: So? There's a mature tea tree here now, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... yeah, but...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: And am I not the White Horse Adeptus?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... yeah?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Is this tea tree then not a manifestation of the White Horse Adeptus's will?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're... not wrong, but again, there's something not quite right about this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm. Maybe this'll become another mystical adepti tale recorded in their family history.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: That would be marvelous.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hehe, Paimon thinks so too... Hey, {NICKNAME} — Zibai seems to be doing much better now, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe being outside is good for her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Paimon bets that's why Zhongli chose to send her on this errand...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why don't we continue showing her around Liyue?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh! That's a great idea! We've already shown her Liyue Harbor, Yilong Wharf, and Qiaoying Village — how about we head to Qingce Village next?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Qingce? That name sounds familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The scenery there is really beau— pretty, too. It's the perfect sightseeing spot! How about we show you around?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: I must say, I have been mightily impressed by the mountains and waters of Liyue. Please, lead the way, my dutiful guides.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! Let's go...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Paimon can't help feeling like we've forgotten something...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Pay it no mind — I've already forgotten more than you will ever know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright... Eh, if we forgot something, it can't have been that important to begin with.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Qingce Village, here we come!

talks.objective: Go to Third-Round Knockout and look for Zhongli

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like Zhongli hasn't stopped by for tea today...

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: Hey, are you two looking for your friend? Try going up that way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is Zhongli up that way?

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: No... but that young lady who was dressed up as the White Horse Adeptus the other day is — she's your friend, right?

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: I just saw her head toward Wanmin Restaurant. I was wondering why she was eating alone, but then you two showed up hot on her heels.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! What luck — we were just on our way to find her! But... what's she doing at Wanmin Restaurant?

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: I have no idea — I said hello, but she completely ignored me.

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: She couldn't have forgotten who I am, right? I mean, we're kindred spirits, aren't we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... maybe she's still half-asleep... Her brain might be a little fuzzy!

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: Oh! That makes sense... I was wondering why her eyes were so red.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Her eyes were red? That doesn't sound good...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We need to find out what's happening.

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: You young people, staying up all night because you think you're invincible... Look at your friend, missing out on sleep so she can pretend to be the White Horse Adeptus. That's where that leads you, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: A word to your friend from someone who's older and wiser — she really needs some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Hehe... Paimon wouldn't be so certain about the older and wiser part...

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: What was that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: N—Nothing! We'll make sure to pass on your message!

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: Hurry along then, oh and don't forget to come back and check out my Rex Lapis cosplay when you're done!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Where's the proprietor? Come out and see me at once!

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: Xiangling and Chef Mao aren't here right now. What can I help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: And who might you be?

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: My name is Shenhe. I work here at Wanmin Restaurant.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Shen... he... Shenhe...? Are you that Crane Adeptus who loves planting Mint?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Hmph, it's been a few days. Have you improved your gardening skills? Did you manage to cover the slopes with Mint?

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: Mint? I don't know anything about Mint... but I am familiar with Qingxin and Glaze Lilies.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Hah! Already casting Mint from your mind! How can a practitioner of self-cultivation be so fickle, chasing after every new plant that catches their eye?

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: I'm not sure I get what you mean...

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: Are you delirious from hunger? Would you like something to eat?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Shenhe! White Horse Ad— Zibai! So this is where everyone is... Hahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon... It's been a long time. Happy Lantern Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Happy Lantern Rite, Shenhe.

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: Is this customer a friend of yours?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I guess you could say that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't mind her, Shenhe, she's just a little cranky, because... Uh... she didn't sleep well last night and she's only just woken up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look how red her eyes are!

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: I see... In that case, Miss Zibai, I have a tonic here infused with Qingxin. It's cool and soothing when applied to the eyes. Would you like to try a few drops?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Stop right there!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Who are you two noisy children?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Have you forgotten about us already?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're your guides.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Guides...?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Hmm... Yes, I seem to recall something about some guides...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Ah, yes, now I remember! What luck — I was just looking for someone to show me the way to Yilong Wharf.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh! Is she starting to come around?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why do you want to go to Yilong Wharf?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Someone requested my help in purchasing some tea leaves. I was informed they have discounted prices during the festival and that I shall get a good deal there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tea leaves...? This sounds like Zhongli's doing... He sure knows how to get people running errands for him!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Has Zhongli started buying discounted tea?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Your friend, Rex— Zhongli, initially requested the most expensive tea.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: But then a young lady in a hexagram hat mentioned he'd burned through the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's yearly expenses at an exhibition a few days ago.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: As such, he is only permitted to buy items that are discounted this month.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! That's his boss, Hu Tao! It's about time she realized the problem and put a stop to his spending sprees.

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: Oh, I see. So that's why you're here. Unfortunately, Wanmin Restaurant doesn't sell tea leaves... If you're truly in need, I could gather some wild tea from the mountain slopes.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: You don't sell tea leaves? But I remember your boss, Miss Lu, saying that she owns tea fields.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You really should get some rest... The person you're talking about isn't the boss of Wanmin Restaurant! She's just like you — she came here to eat!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Is that so? Life really is full of surprises.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What surprises!? Your brain really is as gooey as a pack of Slimes... Paimon can't believe Zhongli entrusted you with going all the way to Yilong Wharf and buying tea...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why don't we show you the way to Yilong Wharf?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: That would be excellent, my dutiful guides.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Ah, yes, Miss Crane, I apologize profusely for my improper behavior just now. Please forgive me.

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: I completely understand. Master often says that the human body is like a mechanism in need of regular maintenance. When a person cannot rest at night, they are sure to become irritable and on edge.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Miss Crane... You appear reasoned and compassionate on the surface, yet I sense dark forces churning within your spiritual core... Those red ropes you wear are what bind them, am I correct?

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: ...You can sense that?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Indeed. I also sense that with your strength, you might try undoing one or two of those bonds when training.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Untie Shenhe's ropes? Wouldn't that be risky...?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Though the use of red ropes to bind the soul is a wondrous technique, practitioners must eventually learn to break free from external aids and look within themselves for restraint.

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: Master has told me similar things, but I... I am not ready yet.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Your self-cultivation has progressed far enough.

dialogues.speaker: Shenhe
dialogues.text: Then I will seek further guidance from my master.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: If you still have doubts, you can find me at the Baiju Guesthouse. I'll be taking up residence there for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: For now, my dutiful guides, let us be off.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Weren't we going to Yilong Wharf? How did we end up on this mountain?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Is that small town over there not Yilong Wharf? I sense a familiar scent wafting through the air.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're right... Except for the smell part. Paimon doesn't smell anything.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: That is because... this scent is the essence of jade, which can nourish the spirit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Yeah, Chenyu Vale does have a lot of jade... but Paimon didn't think jade smelled like, y'know, anything...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Naturally, this has reminded me of something.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? And what's that?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: A few simple tricks for mastering one's power.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is that thing!?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: I'm sure you've been to Yilong Wharf many times before. But I wonder if you've done so while cruising through the air?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: You've been such dutiful, dedicated guides, so allow me to offer this fresh experience as recompense.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Please, step in.

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: I should hurry home and pray to the White Horse Adeptus. May she bless me, such that I never encounter such customers again.

talks.objective: Go to where the tea merchant is

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: Welcome! Please have a look around. We only sell teas of the finest quality, sourced directly from Qiaoying Village. Right now, we're offering a special discount for Lantern Rite!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look over there! Discounted tea!

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: Dear customers, are you looking to purchase some tea leaves?

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: I can see from your bearing that you are no ordinary customers — my humble shop has some exquisite teas that should satisfy your more refined tastes.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: We're not here for quality — we're looking for a discount.

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: Discount? Well, that's a coincidence! Our Sunglo Tea is on sale right now. A special festive offer!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Something about the name of that tea sounds familiar to Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: Buy three boxes of Sunglo Tea during the festival to get ten percent off. Buy four, get twenty percent off. Buy ten b—

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Buy ten boxes, get fifty percent off?

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: That's right, ten boxes at half price! Have you been to our shop before, by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon's definitely heard this spiel before!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Three, four, ten...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Ten, twenty, fifty...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zibai, what are you muttering about...?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: When purchasing three, four, or ten boxes... the corresponding discounts are ten, twenty, and fifty percent...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: The intervals between the two sets of numbers are 1 and 6, and 10 and 30...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look! Her eyes turned blue! That's gotta be a first...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: If the differences between intervals remain equal, the interval after six should be six plus the difference between six and one, which is eleven. Similarly, after thirty, the next interval should be fifty...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Therefore, extrapolating upward, the next two numbers in each set should be twenty-one and one hundred.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... you're making Paimon's head spin... Those numbers... What do they mean?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: They mean that if we buy twenty-one boxes of Sunglo Tea, we should get a 100% discount.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A 100% discount!? You mean we'll get 'em for free!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That is what she means.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh, there was a pattern to the discounts... Is... is that right?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: The pattern we speak of is mathematics, little one. A pattern that is always right.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's amazing! You're a shopping genius, Zibai! But wait... something feels off here...

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: *cough*... I had no idea our shop's discounts were tied to the laws of nature... I've learned so much from you, dear customer...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: No need to thank me. Now, please give us our twenty-one boxes of free tea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—Wait!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon just realized what it is that's not right...

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: It took you long enough...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We got the short end of the stick!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Think about it — if we don't have to pay when buying twenty-one boxes, then if we buy even more, the vendor should be paying us money instead, right?

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: Huh...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Zibai, work this one out! If we buy a hundred boxes, we'd make loads of money, wouldn't we?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: It stands to reason.

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: Wait a moment, dear customers... don't you think you're haggling a little too hard?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: You are the one dictating the discounts. We're simply extrapolating the numerical patterns within. As such, we are hardly haggling.

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: Uhm... You have a point... However... Ah, aha! That's right!

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: I'm so sorry, I just remembered... My supplier didn't come today, so we don't have any tea after all...

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: Such a shame... Terribly sorry about this... awful, awful luck... Ahahem...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Where can we find your supplier?

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: Uhm... Well...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Not to fret. We'll save you the effort and go straight to the source ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: Uhm... W—Well you see, dear client, the supplier's discount isn't as generous as ours. You won't be able to get the same price from them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Does that mean they won't pay us for taking their tea?

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: Ahahem... They might not even offer you a 100% discount...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: How very unfortunate. Nevertheless, as the original supplier, they must offer some sort of discount.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Besides, we're not looking to make money — we just want a good deal.

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: W—Well... that's great. My suppliers are all tea farmers from Qiaoying Village... You can go ask around the village — but please don't say I sent you...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Do not worry, we appreciate your generosity.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Referring customers to your business partners, even choosing to remain anonymous — the demeanor of a true gentleman, indeed. Your business will surely prosper.

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: I hope you're right, haha...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Then let us head to Qiaoying Village. Do you know the way, my guides?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course. Just follow us!

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: *sigh*... What otherworldly beings were those? Thank the heavens I managed to send them on their way...

dialogues.speaker: Fenglian
dialogues.text: I should hurry home and pray to the White Horse Adeptus. May she bless me, such that I never encounter such customers again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Here we are — Qiaoying Village!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: The mountains and waters are pristine — they embody the beauty of heaven and earth.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's a good-looking place, alright, but it's hard to enjoy the scenery when Paimon can't stop thinking about all that tea-buying Mora we're missing out on.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Should fate dictate, Mora will find its way to you sooner or later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Morax certainly finds us often enough. He even sought us out in person this Lantern Rite...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Hehe. For now, let's look around and see if any tea farmers are selling their crop.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: We'll be able to see more clearly from up high. Let's take to the sky and enjoy the beautiful scenery while we're at it.

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Li
dialogues.text: We should plant cucumbers!

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Tian
dialogues.text: We should plant canolas!

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Li
dialogues.text: We should plant cucumbers — they're easy to sell!

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Tian
dialogues.text: We should plant canolas — the flowers are pretty!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: What are you arguing about, little ones?

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Tian
dialogues.text: We're deciding what to plant in our field once Lantern Rite is over.

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Li
dialogues.text: Yeah! Dad gave us a small plot of land to grow our own crops. He said we can keep all the Mora we get from selling them.

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Li
dialogues.text: We should plant cucumbers, right? Dad plants cucumbers every year.

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Tian
dialogues.text: We should plant canolas! We can press the seeds for oil — it smells good and sells for a good price.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Ah, an agricultural debate. This should be easy to sort out.

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Tian
dialogues.text: Hmm? Granny, are you a farmer? Could you tell us what to do?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: G—Granny!?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: What did you just call me, you rapscallion?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, her eyes are gonna turn red again...

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Tian
dialogues.text: Uhm, it's just... my Granny smells really nice... and you smell nice too... so...

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Li
dialogues.text: S—Sorry! How about we call you Auntie instead...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Auntie!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just call her Big Sis Zibai.

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Tian
dialogues.text: Oh... alright. Big Sis Zibai, can you help us decide whether we should grow cucumbers or canolas in our field...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Hmph! You little rascals, using priceless land like this just for cucumbers and canolas — what a waste of heaven's gifts!

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Li
dialogues.text: Huh? What should we plant instead?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: With the coming of spring, when all things awaken, the fields should be sown with the five grains.

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Tian
dialogues.text: ...What are those?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: The five grains are life's staples, the heart of the people's table. I notice the people here mostly eat rice, so that is where you should begin.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Based on the local climate and soil, seedlings planted in mid to late spring should produce mature grain within two or three months.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: When autumn comes, you can plant a second crop, with time still to harvest it before the first frost.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: The rice you harvest can be sold at market or kept in your stores. It's a far better choice than cucumbers or canolas.

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Tian
dialogues.text: Oh... but... Big Sister Zibai, I like canolas.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: That's no issue. It is unsuitable for continuous cropping in any case. You can rotate it with rice to maximize your yields.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: After the second rice harvest, around winter time, will be the perfect opportunity to sow their seeds.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: And when they mature in mid to late spring, you shall be just in time to sow the first rice crop of the year in turn.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: This way, your field will sustain balance — rice and canola in a harmonious cycle.

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Tian
dialogues.text: Wow, that means we'll have crops to harvest all year round!

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Li
dialogues.text: W—Wait a minute! If rice and canola take up the whole year, then what about my cucumbers?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: A firefly dares rival the brilliance of the moon? In what twisted universe should cucumbers vie for land with rice!?

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Tian
dialogues.text: B—Big Sis Zibai... You're going to hurt Lil' Li's feelings...

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Li
dialogues.text: *sob* *sob*... Auntie hates cucumbers... Waah! Waah...!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Stop crying this instant! I... I meant that cucumbers are simple enough to grow — there's no need to devote a whole field to them.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Just find an empty corner of your yard, scatter some cucumber seeds in the earth, and before you know it, you'll have a thriving patch of vines.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Cucumbers delight in sunlight and moisture, but they suffer in cold weather. If you wish to plant them this early in the year, you should make sure they're protected from frost.

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Li
dialogues.text: Wow... Is it really that simple? Let's hurry home and get started right away!

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Tian
dialogues.text: Are you really in that much of a rush? Well... thanks, Big Sis Zibai Who's Fierce but Really Good at Farming! We gotta go!

dialogues.speaker: Lil' Li
dialogues.text: Thanks, Big Sis Zibai! See you around!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon never imagined you'd know so much about farming...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: What's so strange about that? The people of Lang-Gan called me the "God of Soil and Grain." Are the fields not made of soil? Is rice not one of the five grains?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, that's true. So, if the God of Soil and Grain is a farming god... that means the White Horse Adeptus must be a farming adeptus, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: When you put it like that, Zibai suddenly seems very down-to-earth.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course the god of farming is down-to-earth!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Mind your tongue, impertinent child! How dare you diminish the lofty bearing of an adeptus!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! You're the one who said the God of Soil and Grain is all about farming!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Enough! It's time for us to take to the skies once more. Join me now — witness the majesty of mountain, water, and field, and broaden your horizons!

talks.objective: Follow the voice to its source

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: I can't help but feel there's something strange about this "friend you haven't seen in ages."

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Strange? Whatever do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Her strangeness defies description! This Miss Zibai is a full-blown enigma, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Hehe, I'm afraid I have no idea what you're talking about.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Aren't you worried about sending her all the way to Yilong Wharf on her own — to buy tea? What if she gets lost?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Where there are people, there are paths.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Now I'm the one with no clue what you're saying...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: ...She can ask for directions.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: And then what?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: She will meet strangers in unfamiliar lands, build friendships, part ways... Hers will be a long journey indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The further the journey, the more footprints one leaves behind. The deeper those footprints, the harder it is for time to erase them.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oh... So you want her to make new friends?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: I see. But from what you say... it sounds as though she's not from Liyue.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I believe she was not, but perhaps she will be.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: You're sounding stranger by the second...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Huh... Oh, over there! Look who's here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hu Tao! Zhongli! What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, fancy meeting in a place like this. Oh my, and Miss Zibai too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We ran into each other by chance.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Sounds like fate to me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe. We were taking Zibai to buy some tea from Yilong Wharf. Zhongli sent her there though she didn't even know the way, and... Oh! Drat! We forgot the tea!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... Paimon knew we were forgetting something!

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Hehe... What's done is done — there's no need to dwell on it. Fresh tea grows with each passing year — let fate deliver it as it wills.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Exactly. You can get tea wherever you go! You're hardly running low now, are you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon feels a lot better now that you've said that... Hehe...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Still, I'm a little confused — if you were buying tea, how did you end up all the way out here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're taking Zibai on a sightseeing tour! We started at Liyue Harbor, stopped in at Yilong Wharf, went sightseeing around Qiaoying Village, made our way to Qingce Village, and now we're here!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Wow, that is quite the itinerary!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... Actually, Paimon thinks it's about time we headed back.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What are you two doing here, Hu Tao, Zhongli?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hehe, I'm here to pay my respects to my ancestors. My dear consultant kindly agreed to join me. It is Lantern Rite, after all — adepti and ancestors should be venerated alike.

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Ancestors... Wait, could you be...

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: ...Are you heir to the Wuwang Kid... or perhaps the Lone Butterfly of the Crimson Flame?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! Have you got all your memories back!?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Huh? Miss Zibai, you know about the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and the Eight Adepts?

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: I happened to hear a storyteller expound on the Sanctification of Tao Dou.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Lots of people know that story, sure, but very few can discern my family lineage from just a glance.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Well, Zhongli, your friend here really is quite something!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Unfortunately, there's no time to dally right now — we have a hill to climb. Perhaps once today is done, we can find time to chat over tea, recite poetry, and admire the moon?

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: That would be wonderful, Director Hu.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Oh, and before we go, you've been traipsing around all day. I suggest you stop off at the Wangshu Inn on your way back for a good night's rest. Wouldn't do to exhaust yourselves, hmm?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thanks for the advice.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Don't mention it!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Alright, we'll take our leave now. See you later!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hu Tao's so thoughtful! Why don't we follow her advice and stay at the Wangshu Inn tonight?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Zibai, you can see the whole of Dihua Marsh from up there — the view's amazing! Plus, you can sample Smiley Yanxiao's cooking!

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Wangshu... An intriguing name. It couldn't hurt to check it out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Awesome! Let's go!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why didn't you say so earlier, then!?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Is that towering structure Wangshu Inn?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure is! We can take the lift up from over there!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Hehe, always walking the path long-trodden — does retracing others' footsteps not tire you?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Come on, get in, we'll fly to the top.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew! This is the first time Paimon's ever flown up to Wangshu Inn on a chariot! Everything's so different when you're up high...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Wangshu... Wangshu... Like Moon Lanterns and Xiao Lanterns... Might it all be a coincidence...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? What's a coincidence?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Do you not know what "Wangshu" means?

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Wangshu can refer to the moon, but its original meaning is actually...

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: The goddess who rides the bright moon's chariot.

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: And you must be... the Conqueror of Demons?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Xiao! Paimon was wondering if we'd disturbed you by flying down from the sky.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Not at all — I sensed an unusual presence long before you arrived, though I didn't expect it to be you in a flying chariot.

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Ah, a witness at last.

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: I was starting to think we should fly a bit lower — t'would be awfully dull if no one ends up marveling at my lofty bearing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No need, no need! This is already showy enough!

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Hehe, I'm not one to do good from the shadows, as Rex Lapis is wont to do.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Then you must be...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She's the White Horse Adeptus.

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Nay. I'm only cosplaying as the White Horse Adeptus, in truth.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Cosplaying? What's that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Ignore her nonsense, she's the genuine article, the one-and-only, completely authentic White Horse Adeptus. It's just...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Xiao, did Zhongli say anything about her being a teensy bit... not quite right...

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: ...Mental instability, perhaps?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did Zhongli tell you that!?

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: No, this is my own speculation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, you've pretty much hit the nail on the head! It's like her brain's filled with a bunch of Slimes right now, all gloopy and messy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's a hot-tempered Pyro Slime... a math-obsessed Hydro Slime... and a mischievous little Anemo Slime...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But don't tell her Paimon said that, or she'll come and tell us all off.

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: You white-haired rascal! Do you think I can't hear you!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-oh, we're in for it now!

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Hmm... White Horse Adeptus... You must be weary from your journey. Why not take a rest?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, yes, yes, yes! You must be hungry, right, Zibai? How about we get some food... Haha... The chef here is incredible... Hehe...

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Mm! It's so hot... So spicy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you okay? Do you want Paimon to get you some water?

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Ahem... Don't worry about me... I just need to pace myself.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: So... regarding your friend and her... condition, does even the Lord of Geo have no solution?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Zhongli said we should wait, and she'll get better on her own. But who knows how long that's gonna take...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He says her three spirits have only just merged and have yet to settle.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Is that why her personalities change so easily?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks that has something to do with her Three Deadly Selves. Zhongli told us that the Deadly Selves are impure, affecting living things that get too close...

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Hmm, the White Horse Adeptus's remnant spirit was attached to the Deadly Selves for a long time... It makes sense that her temperament and memories would have been influenced by them...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... Paimon still doesn't really understand what the Three Deadly Selves actually are...

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Paimon, as you do not practice self-cultivation, I cannot help you fully understand, but you can think of them simply as emotions and desires.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: The act of "Severing the Three Deadly Selves" is a means of exorcising wicked desires and cultivating one's true self. I believe other nations have similar practices — in Sumeru, it is known as Shattering Atmagraha.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! So it's about emotions, desires, and attachments, that sort of thing!

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: It includes those... I wonder, does she still remember what happened in the past?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Some of it, but right now, it's like she was suddenly awakened — like she's still half dreaming.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The half that's still dreaming might remember things, but the half that's awake doesn't quite get it.

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Conqueror of Demons... Are you looking to learn about Rex Lapis's past from me?

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: You are an old friend of his, so please, call me by my name.

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Hehe, but "Conqueror of Demons" sounds so much more imposing.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'd like to know about Zhongli's past too.

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: In days of yore, he was... the Lord of Geo, Heaven's Star.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? You said the same thing the day you came back! B—But, what does it mean?

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Mmm... I'm afraid I can't remember.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Did you really forget, or are you just pretending so you don't have to tell?

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Why not ask Rex Lapis himself? Whether I've forgotten might be up for debate, but I am certain he remembers.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Hmm... He must have his reasons for not raising the past, and you likely have similar concerns. I shouldn't have asked.

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: An answer that suits your style, General Alatus. Now that we're on the subject, though, I suddenly remembered something...

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Which is?

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: In the distant past, there was a feast, which I attended. I faintly recall the Lord of Geo also being present that day...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! And then? What happened?

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Among the dishes served, there was one that could be found in every household throughout Lang-Gan at the start of spring — a dish called "Flavor of Spring."

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: I suddenly remembered the recipe for this dish.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Is that it!?

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Yes. Since it's Lantern Rite here in Liyue, why don't I make some for you to try?

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: ...That sounds... good.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! It might not have been the story Paimon was hoping for... but this looks deeelicious!

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: The spring breeze stirs — now is the perfect time to savor this dish.

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: My dutiful guides have gone to great trouble to show me around Liyue, and even the Conqueror of Demons has graced us with his presence. I feel deeply honored — this Flavor of Spring is my way of expressing my gratitude.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: There's no need for such grand words...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I have a gift for you, too.

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: ...What's this?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! It's that broken jade token from the antiques exhibition!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I believe this belongs to you, yes?

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Hehe, indeed, this was once an adeptal treasure of mine. I'm amazed it ended up in your hands. Alas, it serves little purpose now in its fractured state. Please, keep it as a memento.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that's a shame... Can't we fix it?

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: This is the way of the world — once jade is broken, it can never be made whole.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Then... what about forging a new one?

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Hehe... That is a good point — that it has ended up in your hands must be a message from fate.

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: I could try to craft it into a little trinket for you. One that might prove useful on your journey.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh? What sorta trinket?

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Hehe, it's just a passing thought, one that will require the right opportunity. I'll think about it more when the time comes.

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Now that we've had our fill, we should get some rest. Tomorrow we return to Liyue Harbor, where I'll have need of your guidance once more.

response.speaker: Zibai
response.text: Not bad. You're clearly much sharper than your diminutive companion.

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Qiqi, the Lantern Rite is almost over. Do you remember how to make a Xiao Lantern?

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: #Morning, split bamboo, {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Then get silk, make Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: You've got it all mixed up again!

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: ...They're here again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yaoyao! Looking good in that new outfit, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Hey, it's Paimon! Hehe, Dr. Baizhu gave this to me as a gift. How does it suit me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It suits you very well — you look adorable.

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! What happened for Baizhu to suddenly give you a brand-new outfit, Yaoyao?

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Dr. Baizhu is thanking Yaoyao... for teaching me to make Xiao Lanterns...

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Qiqi and I were just playing together! Dr. Baizhu's too kind.

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah, take a look at this! Dr. Baizhu gave me these clothes, but it was Qiqi who wove this little basket!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that's beautiful! When did you become so good with your hands, Qiqi?

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: I learned to make Xiao Lanterns... thanks to Yaoyao...

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: I also made a wish...

dialogues.speaker: Lu Weng
dialogues.text: What do I always say? The White Horse Adeptus answers prayers! Come, help this old man make an offering in thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Huh? Mr. Lu? What did you pray for?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Weng
dialogues.text: For my idiot son to finally come to his senses and not change Baiju Guesthouse's name — which he has!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? He's keeping the old name?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Weng
dialogues.text: Listen to this — my granddaughter planted a tea seedling in our village just a few days ago...

dialogues.speaker: Lu Weng
dialogues.text: She made a prayer to the White Horse Adeptus to help it grow. Overnight, her seedling flourished into a mature tea tree!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... haha... That sure does sound like a miracle...

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Could the White Horse Adeptus really have helped it grow?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Weng
dialogues.text: Of course she did! O, White Horse Adeptus... How blessed is our family, over whom you keep watch!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Truly, this is an extraordinary miracle. You must record it in your family history without delay!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Weng
dialogues.text: Of course... Huh? Is that you, Miss... Zibai?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Indeed. I have a long-term booking at your guesthouse.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Weng
dialogues.text: Yes, yes, yes, I recall. Mr. Zhongli said to charge your expenses to the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, if I remember correctly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That Zhongli... Always making trouble for poor Hu Tao.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Weng
dialogues.text: Hmm... I noticed when you were here last that you bear a striking resemblance to the pictures of the White Horse Adeptus in my family history — you both have golden eyes...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Perhaps fate has had a hand in our meeting.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Weng
dialogues.text: And a glad meeting it is, Miss Zibai! Now, why don't I gift you some tea from my garden to celebrate this encounter?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Weng
dialogues.text: We grow Sunglo Tea there, and it has quite a reputation throughout Yilong Wharf. I hope you will accept it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Sunglo "Buy-Ten-Boxes-Get-Half-Off" Tea's back on the menu!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Weng
dialogues.text: Buy ten boxes, get half off? Don't be silly, this is a gift. It's free!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woohoo... Nice!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Hehe, thank you so much, Boss Lu.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Weng
dialogues.text: There's no need to thank me. You're a visitor from out of town, which makes you an honored guest — make yourself at home.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Weng
dialogues.text: Lantern Rite may have ended, but the streets are still bustling with activity.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Weng
dialogues.text: Make sure to take everything in, meet some new friends, and enjoy your time here!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Weng
dialogues.text: And that goes for you kids, as well. Happy Lantern Rite!

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Got it, Mr. Lu!

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Happy... Lantern Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! Happy Lantern Rite, everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Happy Lantern Rite indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, Lu Xiangxiang! It really is you!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: #Huh? Paimon, {NICKNAME}, and the "White Horse Adeptus"! Fancy seeing you here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehehe, the White Horse Adeptus has a name now! You can call her Zibai!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: And you are...?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Wait... I remember now, you're...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't say anything about food poisoning or fish!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: You're... the young lady who wanted to rise above the rest, are you not?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Haha... Yes, that's me, but I'm in a bit of a state right now — at best, I can say I've... fallen below them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fallen below them? What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Like I said the last time we met, I'm being punished according to family rules.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: My father, mother, grandfather, grandmother, other grandfather, other grandmother...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! That's a lot of family members...

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Yeah, and on the night of Lantern Rite, they held a family meeting to discuss my situation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So they do care about you!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: There's no doubt they care, but they think that since I caused all that trouble in Liyue Harbor, it shows I can't be trusted on my own. They decided to ground me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ground you?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Yeah, though they're not confining me to my room. Instead, I have to personally nurture a tea seedling until it grows big enough to be sold at market.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, a tiny little tea baby! Do they want you to experience what it's like to be a parent?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: It's supposed to cultivate my character and temperament. They say this will help me calm down and reflect on my issues.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened in Liyue Harbor really wasn't your fault... Oh well, at least this punishment doesn't sound too harsh.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... how long will it take for the little tea baby to grow?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Actually, I don't know. I've never grown a tea tree before...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: It usually takes two or three years.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Two or three years!?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Yes, the tea in this garden requires two or three years to mature.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That long!? Zibai, you're not making this up, are you? How do you know so much about growing tea?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: When the plants thrive and grow — that is the meaning of my name. I can tell at a glance when their season of ripening will come.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Do I really have to waste two or three years here... Why is this happening to me? I'd only just found my direction in life...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you figure out what you could do to make it on your own?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Yes! During the night of Lantern Rite, I heard many people reciting poems from Lang-Gan in praise of the moon. In that moment, I suddenly felt a great sense of pride...

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: I mean, I helped excavate cultural artifacts from Lang-Gan, so I contributed to the revival of these poems, too, right?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: So I decided to stay with the archaeological team. I want to unearth even more history.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: I see... And are you sure that's what you want to do? If you don't achieve anything significant in the years to come, will you still enjoy it?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Yes! Because archaeology gives me that "boom shaka-laka" feeling!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... Did Xiangling teach you that?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's right, I was asking her for advice. She said that if something gives you that boom shaka-laka feeling, then it has to be worth pursuing.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: I immediately thought about how, when I'm excavating in the ruins, I always feel like there's a ghost standing beside me — and not in a spooky way!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: It feels like my great-great-great-great... great-grandmother, patting me on the shoulder and saying, "Keep going! You're about to rediscover some grand ancestral knowledge!"

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That certainly sounds like a boom shaka-laka sort of feeling...

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Right? It feels like I've made some kind of connection with my ancestors... Isn't that amazing?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Since you've made up your mind, you should give it your all.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: And I'd love to... but I'm still grounded.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Run away. Summon up a little boom shaka-laka and leave the tea garden behind — flee this village.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... That might be going a bit far! You don't want to lead others astray, Zibai...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe you can try negotiating with your family.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! Tell them about your great-great-great-great... great-grandmother! She must be the most super-duper ancestor to have ever risen above the rest, right?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: ...I'd be better off telling them about the White Horse Adeptus — after all, she's the supreme riser-above-the-rest who saved my great-great-great-great... great-grandmother!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Then it's settled. Tell your family that your decision has my blessing.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Uhm... thank you, Zibai... but I don't think cosplay is going to work on them — they won't listen.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: They don't need to listen — you need only follow the rules they've set out for you.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: As I'm sure you know, some ancient texts refer to the White Horse Adeptus as the daughter of Time.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: My family history contains such records... but what of it?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: If the White Horse Adeptus were to manipulate time to make your tea seedling grow overnight, then you'd be free, correct?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that how it works!?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: If the White Horse Adeptus were to really get involved, my grandfather would let me leave right away, but... *sigh*... Who really believes that she'd show up and help?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: It's not as if you have any other options. Why not try calling out for help? It won't cost you any Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: ...Guess I might as well... I've got no better ideas anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: White Horse Adeptus — if you can hear me, please save me from my predicament!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: *sigh* Nothing happened... as expected.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Hehe, perhaps the White Horse Adeptus has already heard your prayer. Why not come back here tomorrow and take a look?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: By then, the seedling you planted may well have grown into a thriving tea tree.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Thank you, Zibai, for trying to comfort me. I do feel better now, kinda.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... can... can she really do something like that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm curious to find out.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Oh, it's getting late. Why don't you all stay at my house tonight? My family may be strict with me, but they're always welcoming to guests!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounds great! Let's get some sleep and then come back here tomorrow to see if our tea baby has grown!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wonders how the White Horse Adeptus is getting along. Maybe we should check in on her? We can ask Zhongli where she is.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look! Paimon thinks she saw a tea vendor over there!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Very well, let's take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look! There's someone in that tea field, and they look kinda familiar... Wait, is that Lu Xiangxiang?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: And who is that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! You'll remember her once you see her up close.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! We've arrived at Wuwang Hill! The atmosphere just turned spooky...
I can't help but feel there's something strange about this "friend you haven't seen in ages."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Paimon thought she heard someone's voice. Let's head down and check it out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are we really gonna fly up to Wangshu Inn? Isn't that a bit showy? All the guests are gonna see us.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Is that a bad thing? To be able to witness an adeptus — this will surely add to the inn's appeal, not to mention the room prices. The owner will thank us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You seem to really like showing off your powers...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Hehe, this inn's architecture is incredible, and the surrounding countryside radiates a picturesque charm. No wonder the new proprietor of the Baiju Guesthouse thinks he can't compete and has decided to change his own establishment's name.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The new proprietor? Ah, you mean Lu Xiangxiang's dad! So you know about that, too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Personally, Paimon thinks he should go with something like "Rex's Rest." That's a contender's name if Paimon's ever heard one!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: A fitting name indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you think the guesthouse should change its name, too? Paimon kinda thought you'd say something like, "Such sacrosanct traditions must never change."

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Time flows ever onward. Why should the rules of yesterday be carried forward into the world of tomorrow? The people of today should determine what is to be kept.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. You're not as old-fashioned and stuffy as Paimon thought!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: The years ebb and flow, seas recede to reveal fields... In the vastness of time, I am but a wild horse in a boundless sea of dust.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Even Rex Lapis, having waded through the waters of the river of time, is not quite the same as before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Zhongli? What was he like before...?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: That is another story for another time.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: We have arrived.
